## Start with context

Ask why the image appears beside the surrounding text. Describe the information or action it contributes.

The simulated editorial dataset below lets you compare the quantitative
relationship communicated by a Chart with its exact data table. The values are
illustrative, not evidence about a real publishing team.

<Chart
  title="Average published and reviewed lessons per editor"
  description="Average published and reviewed lesson counts per editor are compared for June and July."
  howToRead="Read months from left to right and compare each pair of bars."
  takeaway="Reviews kept pace in June but lagged behind publishing in July."
  xAxis={{ label: "Month", unit: "month" }}
  yAxis={{ label: "Average lessons per editor", unit: "lesson" }}
  series={[
    { name: "Published", values: [{ x: "June", y: 1.001 }, { x: "July", y: 3.003 }] },

  ]}
  source={{

  }}

<KnowledgeCheck
  type="single"
  prompt="What should determine an image description?"
  outcomes={["identify-image-purpose"]}
  options={[
    {
      id: "file-name",
      text: "Its file name",
      feedback: "A file name identifies the asset, but it does not explain the image's purpose in this context.",
    },
    {
      id: "purpose-in-context",
      text: "Its purpose in context",
      feedback: "The purpose identifies the information a screen-reader user needs from this image.",
    },
    {
      id: "pixel-dimensions",
      text: "Its pixel dimensions",
      feedback: "Pixel dimensions describe the file, not the meaning the image contributes.",
    },
  ]}
  answer="purpose-in-context"
  explanation="The surrounding context determines which information a screen-reader user needs from the image."
/>
